function: Joint channel estimation (MOMP) and user-array calibration by dictionary learning, then geometric localization; the learned part refines DoA and channel estimates. p. 3, p. 9
system: 60 GHz, 1 GHz bandwidth; hybrid BS 8x8 UPA with 8 RF chains, MS 4x4 UPA with 4 RF chains; passive reflecting RIS, 16x16 or 32x32. p. 12
method: Classical MOMP sparse recovery plus dictionary learning (method of optimal directions, alternating minimization with LS denoising), unsupervised; no neural network. p. 8, p. 11
data_channel: Wireless InSite ray-traced indoor factory channels, 100 random MS locations; random mutual coupling and gain/phase errors added; realistic coupling in one test. p. 12, p. 14
test_conditions: No separate training and test sets described: one indoor factory scenario with 100 random MS locations; RIS size, coupling model and transmit power varied. p. 12-15
baselines: None from the literature; only the same pipeline before dictionary learning, BS-MS versus RIS-MS channel, and 16x16 versus 32x32 RIS. p. 13-14
metrics: CDFs of DoD and DoA error, TDoA error, channel estimation NMSE and localization error; mean NMSE and localization error versus transmit power. p. 13-15
complexity: Big-O order of the MOMP-based estimator (39) and of DoA recovery, compared with OMP; cost of the dictionary-learning iterations not given. p. 9-10
openness: Dataset github.com/WiSeComLab/RIS-ray-tracing and code github.com/WiSeCom-Lab/RIS-localization, refs [65], [66]. p. 3, p. 16
q1_support: p. 12: "We consider a ray tracing simulation implemented with Wireless InSite software for channel generation in an indoor factory environment". The authors release the dataset ([65], p. 3). It is not DeepMIMO, 3GPP or measured data: counted as another public ray-tracing dataset, for the reviewer to confirm.
q2_support: p. 12: "The location of the MS is randomly generated 100 times at a height of mz = 1.5m." One indoor factory scenario with no separate training and test sets. RIS size, coupling model (p. 14) and transmit power (p. 15) are varied, but the paper never says a dictionary learned in one condition is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 13: "we observe that the DoA estimation error is high for all cases before the dictionary learning algorithm is applied". Only the pipeline without dictionary learning (an ablation of the method) is compared; no published non-learned or learned method is a baseline.
q4_support: p. 10: "the overall computational complexity order of the proposed algorithm can be simply expressed by (39)". This is the Big-O order of the MOMP-based estimator and DoA recovery, compared with OMP; the dictionary-learning iterations are not costed.
q5_support: p. 3: "The channel dataset and the code used to obtain the simulation results are available to the research community in [65] and [66], respectively." Links on p. 16: github.com/WiSeComLab/RIS-ray-tracing (data) and github.com/WiSeCom-Lab/RIS-localization (code).
notes: Checked: p. 1 holds the title and DOI 10.1109/TWC.2024.3486007. Borderline eligibility (rule 3): the channel estimator is classical MOMP sparse recovery and localization is geometric; the only learned part is dictionary learning (method of optimal directions, unsupervised) that calibrates the user-array impairments (p. 11). Included because that learned dictionary is part of the channel estimator; if the reviewer reads it as a calibration or iterative algorithm, exclude as no_learning. Area 2: the learned stage serves channel estimation (NMSE, Figs. 5-7), localization is a downstream geometric step. q1 rests on a public ray-tracing dataset other than DeepMIMO (Wireless InSite, authors' release, p. 3), for the reviewer to confirm.
